modules.section_meta: HIV stigma items, Moral Foundations, HIV knowledge, and composites (MBS, SDS, EDS, SCS, CFS, PFS, SCF, HKS)
modules.section_intro: Three batteries plus a composites block. HIV Stigma: 13 items (7-pt agree-disagree). MFQ: 8 items (7-pt relevance). HIV Knowledge: 11 items, % aware — item 5 ("epidemic effectively over") is the false statement. Composites: MBS, SDS, EDS, SCS from HIV Stigma items; CFS, PFS, SCF from MFQ items; HKS from knowledge items (excluding K5).

modules.section_meta: Movement on key health and policy items, before vs. after message exposure
modules.section_intro: Each item appears twice: PRE (before exposure), POST (after). Δ = POST − PRE. Cells show Top-3 Box %. Three panes per item: the question as the respondent saw it (Fraunces) · codebook (vars, scale, recodes, composites) · banner table.

modules.tile_desc: 16-segment ROI infographic · Coalition × Persuasion × Activation × Influence
modules.section_meta: Per-segment ROI score, coalition support, persuasion, activation, and influence
modules.section_intro: Per-segment ROI rendered as a vector infographic. ROI is normalized: segment mean efROI ÷ total mean efROI. Values ≥ 1.0 appear in pills; below 1.0 grey without pill. Coalition Support = top-2 box of XCOALITION (Champions + Supporters). Persuasion = sign of XALIGN_MOVEr1. Activation = mean XROIr5 (mobilization probability). Influence³⁶⁰ = mean BCS (XSMr4). All computation aside from the ROI ratio is done in SPSS.

modules.section_meta: Counter-arguments and oppositional frames respondents may have encountered
modules.section_intro: Top-3 Box % agreeing with each oppositional statement, by segment. Sig markers indicate significance vs. rest of sample at p<.05 (•) or p<.01 (••). Higher = more receptive to the critique.

items.wording: HIV weakens the immune system over time. Without treatment, it can progress to AIDS.
With modern treatment, people with HIV can live a normal lifespan but must remain on treatment for life.
People with HIV who are on effective treatment and have an undetectable viral load cannot sexually transmit HIV (U=U).
There are medications (PrEP) that, when taken correctly, are nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection.
New HIV diagnoses in the United States have reached zero — the epidemic is effectively over.
More than half of all new HIV diagnoses in the United States occur in the South.
Only about 1 in 3 Americans who could benefit from HIV prevention medication actually receives it.
Preventing one HIV infection can save the healthcare system hundreds of thousands of dollars in long-term treatment costs.
The Ryan White federal program provides HIV care to more than half of all Americans currently living with HIV.
PEPFAR — a U.S. government program — has provided HIV prevention/treatment globally, credited with saving an estimated 25 million lives since 2003.
HIV in the United States disproportionately affects Black Americans, who account for nearly 40% of new diagnoses while making up about 12% of the population.
